classifications.label: Instrumental noise: legitimate thermal, mechanical, and air-current fluctuations at the sensitivity limit of the measurement apparatus
Undetected periodic or quasi-periodic environmental modulation (e.g., building vibration, diurnal temperature cycling, operator technique drift) with period > 10 days or irregular amplitude
Calibration or systematic bias in the period-measurement pipeline (e.g., clock drift, counter error, or photogate misalignment) producing spurious scatter
True physical variation in local gravitational field (micro-seismic, groundwater, or tidal effects) or in the pendulum's moment of inertia (thermal expansion, humidity effects on material properties)
Two physically distinct measurement systems or configurations
Instrumental noise floor differs between apparatus (lab is shielded/damped; obs is not)
Systematic error in pendulum_obs pipeline (electronic timer calibration, photogate alignment, or period-counting algorithm) producing spurious mean and scatter
pendulum_obs baseline not yet established; current 'mean 2.5011' is unstable and will shift when full 10-day baseline is completed

Genuine physical modulation of effective pendulum period (slow environmental forcing, operator technique drift, or uncontrolled parameter coupling) visible only in obs data because lab setup is better isolated

Procedural failure: pendulum_obs baseline was never collected; the 202 'post-baseline' trials are mislabeled and should be treated as unanchored exploratory data until a proper 10-day baseline is established.
Two physically distinct pendulum systems (or configurations) are being measured; pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs are not cross-checks of the same apparatus.

Systematic calibration error in pendulum_obs timer (e.g., clock frequency miscalibrated at setup) produces a fixed proportionality bias; true period is 1.667 beats but obs timer reads it as 2.50 beats.

Environmental noise floor differs sharply between lab (shielded, damped) and obs (exposed to air currents, vibration, thermal gradients); both measure the same pendulum but obs has ~40× larger scatter.
Slow thermal drift, initialization transient, or uncontrolled parameter coupling in pendulum_obs that will stabilize once a full 10-day baseline is collected and equilibration is complete.
Procedural failure: pendulum_obs baseline was never collected; the 202 'post-baseline' trials (days 1–30) are mislabeled unanchored exploratory data.
Two physically distinct pendulum systems (or physical configurations) are being measured; pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs are not redundant cross-checks of the same apparatus.

Systematic calibration error in pendulum_obs timer (e.g., clock frequency miscalibrated at setup, or counter logic runs at 150% nominal speed) produces a fixed proportionality bias; reported obs readings are inflated by ~1.5× the true value.

Environmental noise floor differs sharply between lab (shielded, damped) and obs (exposed to air currents, vibration, thermal gradients); both measure the same pendulum but obs has ~40× larger scatter.

Slow thermal drift, initialization transient, or uncontrolled parameter coupling in pendulum_obs that causes the system to be out of equilibrium during days 1–30; a full 10-day baseline will reveal and allow correction for this drift.
